hints: Look closely at the reaction conditions, cold, dilute manganate(VII) means mild oxidation, not vigorous cleavage.
Focus on the $C=C$ double bond in $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$, this is the part that reacts with the oxidising agent.
Remember what mild oxidation does to an alkene, it adds one $\text{-OH}$ group to each carbon of the double bond to make a diol.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional group that reacts**

Maleic acid is $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$. It has two carboxylic acid groups which are already fully oxidised, and one $C=C$ alkene bond in the middle. The alkene is what will be oxidised.

Key group:
$$\text{-CH=CH-} $$

**Recall what cold, dilute manganate(VII) does**

Cold, dilute, acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ gives mild syn-addition across the double bond. One $\text{-OH}$ adds to each carbon to form a diol.

General rule:
$$\text{RCH=CHR' + [O] + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)-CH(OH)R'}$$

**Apply to maleic acid**

Add $\text{OH}$ to each of the two central carbons, keeping the two $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$ ends unchanged. This gives 2,3-dihydroxybutanedioic acid.

Product:
$$\text{HO}_2\text{CCH=CHCO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{HO}_2\text{CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$$

options.A: This is the diol, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH(OH)CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$. Both carbons of the original $C=C$ have each gained one $\text{-OH}$ group, which is exactly the product of mild oxidation with cold, dilute manganate(VII).
options.B: This is oxalic acid, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCO}_2\text{H}$, a C2 cleavage product. This would come from vigorous oxidative cleavage with hot, concentrated manganate(VII), not cold, dilute conditions. It is the trap for confusing mild and vigorous oxidation.
options.C: This structure has only one $\text{-OH}$ added, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$. Cold manganate(VII) always adds two $\text{-OH}$ groups, one to each carbon. A single addition does not fit the dihydroxylation mechanism.
options.D: This suggests further oxidation to carbonyl groups, $\text{HO}_2\text{CCOCOCO}_2\text{H}$. Cold, dilute conditions stop at the diol stage and do not oxidise further to ketones or cleave the chain. This confuses mild oxidation with strong oxidation.
